findings.title: Queries are interpolated two or three times, duplicating ad hoc label filters on queries with a parser
findings.description:
`runSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)`, but the sub-requests it builds still carry the same `scopedVars` and `filters`. They are interpolated again downstream:

- **Time splitting:** two passes. The second is in `DataSourceWithBackend.query` (`packages/grafana-runtime/src/utils/DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185`), reached via `datasource.runQuery` → `super.query`.
- **Shard splitting:** three passes. `runShardSplitQuery` (`shardQuerySplitting.ts:52`) interpolates, then calls `runSplitQuery` at `shardQuerySplitting.ts:163` with `{ ...request, targets }`, then the backend pass runs.

The updated assertion at `shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:112` (`applyTemplateVariables` called 5 times for one target and four sub-requests) confirms the repetition.

`applyTemplateVariables` is not idempotent for ad hoc filters:

- **Stream selector path:** `addFilterToStreamSelector` de-duplicates via `labelExists` (`modifyQuery.ts:494`), so this path is safe.
- **Label filter path:** `addFilterAsLabelFilter` (`modifyQuery.ts:511-541`) appends unconditionally. `addLabelToQuery` takes this path when the query has a parser and every stream selector has a matcher (`modifyQuery.ts:200-211`).
- **Result:** `{a="b"} | logfmt` with filter `foo=bar` is sent as `{a="b"} | logfmt | foo=`bar` | foo=`bar``, with a third copy under shard splitting.

The duplicated filters should return the same results, but the executed query no longer matches what the user wrote, and it costs a redundant pipeline stage per pass. Before this change the time-splitting path interpolated once, and the shard path never applied filters more than once.

A smaller side effect of the same repetition: a variable whose value itself contains `$name` text matching another variable is now re-expanded on the later passes. This is new for the time-splitting path.

Suggested fix: interpolate exactly once. Either clear `filters` and `scopedVars` on the sub-requests after the up-front pass, or have `runShardSplitQuery` tell `runSplitQuery` the targets are already interpolated.

findings.title: No test covers ad hoc filters through the split paths; the updated assertion pins a call count
findings.description:
- **Missing coverage:** passing `request.filters` is the new behaviour in both entry points, and the shard path previously called `interpolateVariablesInQueries` with no filters at all. No test in either file supplies `filters`, so the duplication above goes undetected.
- **Call-count assertion:** `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` asserts an implementation detail and locks in the redundant passes as expected behaviour.

Add a case with `filters` and a query containing a parser, asserting on the `expr` passed to `runQuery`.

findings.title: New tests interpolate `$__auto` on the frontend, which the real datasource deliberately does not do
findings.description: Both new "Interpolates queries before execution" tests (the other is at `shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:84-101`) mock `templateSrv.replace` to turn `$__auto` into `5m`. The real `applyTemplateVariables` strips `__auto` and the `__range*` variables from `scopedVars` so they are resolved on the backend (`datasource.ts:1111-1113`). The tests still prove the interpolated `expr` and `step` reach `runQuery`, but a user-defined variable would model production behaviour more faithfully.

findings.title: Identical filter-and-interpolate pipeline in both entry points, with different filter order
findings.description: `runShardSplitQuery` filters `expr` then `hide`; `runSplitQuery` (`querySplitting.ts:296-299`) filters `hide` then `expr`; both then apply the same `.map`. The behaviour is equivalent. A shared helper would remove the duplication and give the single-interpolation fix one place to live.

findings.title: Up-front interpolation fixes step-based grouping and query classification
findings.description:
- **Step grouping:** `calculateStep` (`querySplitting.ts:361-372`) previously received a raw `step` such as `$step`, failed the interval regex and fell back to the interval-based step. It now receives the resolved value, so metric queries are grouped and partitioned by their real step.
- **Classification:** `isLogsQuery` and `querySupportsSplitting` now operate on the resolved expression.
- **`$__range` guard:** `isQueryWithRangeVariable` still works, because `applyTemplateVariables` removes `__range*` from the scoped vars it passes to the template service.
- **Shard path:** switching from `interpolateVariablesInQueries` to `applyTemplateVariables` additionally resolves `step` and `legendFormat` and brings ad hoc filters into the selector used to fetch `__stream_shard__` values.
